forges

One client, every forge.

 forges is a TypeScript library for working with issues, pull requests, notifications, checks and webhooks on fourteen forges: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Forgejo, Gitea, Gitee, Azure DevOps, Cursor Origin, Tangled, Pushin.eu, Sourcehut, GitBucket, GitCafe and Upstream. A forge is a service that hosts Git repositories and the collaboration around them. It also reads repositories and their contents from Git hosts without the collaboration, such as Cloudflare Artifacts. Each provider normalises the forge's responses into one data model and declares which operations it supports.

Read the documentation at forges.link.

 install

 

 forges requires Node.js 22.18 or later.

 usage

 

The example above lists the notifications of two forges in a single loop. To go further, the quick start walks you through reading a thread, writing a comment and checking what a forge supports.

 documentation

- Getting started covers installation, import paths and a first call.
- The guides explain authentication, working with several forges, environment variables, webhooks, capabilities, errors, pagination, browser bundles and testing.
- The concepts describe the data model, capabilities, providers and events.
- Each provider page explains how to authenticate and how that forge behaves.
- The reference lists the API, the capability matrix, errors and JSON schemas.
- The examples are small, tested projects that use forges .

 related projects

- @agntn/forges : a TypeScript API for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo and GitBucket, with an MCP server and Pi and OMP extensions for agents.
- git-pkgs/forge : a Go library and CLI for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud, Gerrit and Tangled.

 contributing

Contributions are welcome. The contribution guide explains how to set up the repository and run the checks.

install.title: install
install.html:
pnpm add forges

forges requires Node.js 22.18 or later.

usage.title: usage
usage.html:
import { createForges, forgejo, github } from 'forges'

const forges = createForges([
  github({
    auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN! }
  }),
  forgejo({
    baseUrl: 'https://codeberg.org',
    auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.CODEBERG_TOKEN! }
  }),
])

for await (const notification of forges.notifications.list()) {
  console.log(notification.ref.forge, notification.title)
}

The example above lists the notifications of two forges in a single loop. To go further, the quick start walks you through reading a thread, writing a comment and checking what a forge supports.
